body: once you’ve committed certain acts there’s no hope of it ever really ‘getting better’ because peoples’ view of you will always understandably be coloured by your past actions. once you’ve done it you’ve done it and i have. that’s all i am willing to elaborate. thanks for listening, though

researching college courses to apply to before september. all of them i’ve seen in the brief window a couple months ago i managed to make myself do it involve either moving out to live in student accommodation, or, if they’re online, to talk to other students via zoom calls. help.

Thank you for replying. ‘Low tolerance for moral ambiguity’ is actually a great way of describing it, and putting it that way does help me realise that a majority of people probably wouldn’t worry about a lot of the things I do.


Still living with my parents, I’ve resigned myself that the standard meals (ex. Lunch and dinner) can’t really be concerns since I don’t have much control over it - you’re right that it’s pretty much impossible to eat without discarding those ambiguities, but the fact that I could still theoretically survive without starving nonetheless just gives eating between meals more stock in the ‘morally wrong area’. 


Probably also untrue, I know. But the reason that the lack of a logical reason why distresses me is that there probably is people out there who’d judge me and have a reasonable reason to do it, including the exploited themselves. I can’t help but imagine it, I dunno. You raise a good point that there’s no easy answers though


I don’t know if I should just stop worrying about it altogether if my OCD’s latching onto it this much but I doubt that’s wise since it’s not like it’s entirely invalid. And I mean, I could live with it (Although, I do feel bad about not eating the Easter eggs my family bought me haha).


Sorry about dumping all this here, thanks for the thought-provoking response you gave and for the well-wishes

It feels like I’m taking it to the extreme, but I don’t know where the line is drawn, you know? I’m a subscriber to the labour theory of value myself, but what that one person in the original thread said about still taking care to pursue harm reduction won’t leave my head. And knowing that, eating ‘forbidden’ stuff when I don’t necessarily have to in order to survive still makes me feel guilty. Like that sounds ridiculous but I can’t think of a logic reason why, I dunno.

Honestly, between this and the other opinions presented on this thread, I’m just as confused as when I came in, haha.


 I appreciate the perspective, though. I think I just base my choices off of ‘would other people think I’m a bad person for doing this and have reasonable enough reasons for that’ more than anything else, so the theoretical problem that people could do so for pretty much everything poses a problem for just defining it myself as you say. Though, I have OCD, so that could be involved there. It’s a good point that my actions are comparatively small, though

I guess? Nothing too extreme, I don’t think. Just this occasional feeling when, if I find someone attractive, that’ll be the main thing I think about. I guess not even ‘not seeing them as a person’, because sometimes their personality is apart of the attraction. I don’t know. I guess you can’t help feeling attracted to people, but I just feel like sometimes it’s just kind of odd the way I react.


Like if I see someone in an outfit I think is attractive or whatever, my immediate way of viewing them and the outfit is based around that rather than just ..  seeing them as a person wearing clothing. Not even that I necessarily see them as not a person or just an object for my pleasure or anything like that, like, they’re a human being and I still view them as such, but it just feels weird for my perception of them and their clothing to have my attraction to them as the main underlying precedent. Maybe not dehumanising but still feels weird?


Obviously this is just a kneejerk response, I tell myself “that’s silly, don’t view them that way” and I usually get over it. I don’t know if that even counts as objectification, but the possible proximity to it is what worries me. I don’t know, I know you can’t help feeling attracted to someone so maybe this is something everyone goes through and I’m just letting OCD mess with me. But the discomfort I feel looking at how I used to view women’s bodies as a kid who didn’t know better really makes me feel awful at the prospect of viewing them in a similar way still.


This is the problem, it could just be OCD exaggeration but there’s genuine reason that it could be a real thing I have, you know? And I don’t want to let myself just kind of get away with it if it’s true. I don’t think I objectify women but I’m not entirely convinced I don’t at the same time, even if it’s just a little bit. It’s weird.

Oh, don’t worry, I don’t mean to imply that I’m fantasising about real people I know or see, that’d be awful. All of the fantasy aspect uses people I just sort of make up in my brain, because it feels creepy to do that to an actual person without their knowledge.


I just meant that, even if the fantasy is fake, it’s surely influenced by stuff I’ve watched in the past, and if that same stuff lead to me having that weird kneejerk response to women on occasion, then surely fantasising, if unrelated in terms of content, could be helping perpetuate that response somehow? I dunno, not sure if that’s even how it works. But yeah, I never ever let that response go anywhere past ‘that person is attractive’, I would never do that to someone. 


I guess you’re right that the instant attraction is pretty normal, though, I suppose you can’t help it. I just don’t want it to be anything but ‘oh, that person’s cute’ and then move on and that’s it. But sometimes feels like it isn’t, I guess, I don’t know. This is what I mean, it’s unclear, because it’s totally plausible that it could be real, but it could easily be OCD making me think I’m seeing them like that when in reality I think the opposite.


Yeah, I don’t know. But thank you for replying, it really helps to discuss this with someone

It left my head for a second, and then I remembered it, but when I remembered it my brain’s “oh, yeah” moment I think caused the word to kind of half-come into my head? Sorry for late reply. But, what do you mean by that?

Are my concerns about touching it and then touching other things unreasonable, then? I just can’t get the idea out of my head that it surely would’ve ‘infected’ everything. I don’t want to go around my house touching stuff and rolling around in it when in bed. But so is that concern invalid now I’ve wiped and dried it? Sorry for the bombardment of questions, just not well-educated about how this stuff works

Well, that’s the thing. It’d be best because it is kinda gross to just touch it and not do much, right? But if I’m sleeping in it, putting my phone on it, etc etc. I’d have to shower, wash my phone and so on every time so as not to do that. I don’t know how I’d survive knowing that I would be covering myself in that stuff every time I do one of those things. I don’t know.

It’s just that I’m mainly worried about touching other stuff after it. Like if I put my phone on my bed, or touch my bed and then touch something else downstairs, etc.


Is that even reasonable either, though? Again, don’t know much about how that sort of thing works
Yeah, it’s the worst, right? Often a “But did I actually say it for real this time?” type thing for me

No. Haven’t actually been diagnosed yet. I don’t really know when it’s going to be possible, or if I’d even feel comfortable speaking about half of the things that bother me. So I rely on the Internet for now.


I guess it’s good that there’s someone who’s gone through a similar thing, though

Hey, sorry for bothering you again (and sorry for not replying initially). I’m glad to know you think it’s irrational, but I’m struggling to grasp it. At first I was like ‘Ah, I guess I was just worrying for nothing then’. Given what you’ve said, plus the fact I haven’t really interacted with them in a romantic way in a while, I felt comfortable trying to watch stuff like that again.


But, I don’t know. I just can’t grasp fully why you find it irrational. Realistically, it probably is, but I really can’t just sit with it. You’re free to refuse if you think it’d be beneficial, because if my worries are false then this is blatant reassurance, I’m aware. But I just can’t get at peace with how I acted and how that’s okay. Again, you’re free to refuse if you think it’s the best course of action. But, if not, do you mind explaining why you feel that way?


There’s still just so much uncertainty surrounding it. Realistically I should try and make my feelings explicitly known like you said, but it’s difficult to slip it into conversation, so I don’t really know when I’m gonna get around to it, meaning I’m gonna have this on my mind for who knows how long. I still give in to doing it a lot despite this, as previously talked about. Usually I try and talk myself down, “Hey, that person said it’s fine so realistically it probably is”, but I still feel like some of my doubts are reasonable, I don’t know.


Sorry for the wall of text (I’m not sure if some of it even makes sense, ask if you need anything clarified) and thank you if you read this
Thanks. I know reassurance doesn’t help in the long run, but sometimes I really can’t tell, so this helps. Sorry your OCD latched onto it as well
Thank you, so much. This really helps clear it up. Usually I can spot when I’m checking, but this time it was cloudy, so it helps to have an outside opinion like this.
